title: Guess the body part
question: What are you looking at?
lines: Comment the second you know what this is.
We're zoomed all the way in on one bone. Watch it pull back.
What are you looking at?
Those holes let the sacral nerves leave the bone.
The coccyx is the small tail below it, not this.
It's B. The sacrum.
Fun fact: it starts as five vertebrae that fuse after about age 20.
why: B) The sacrum, seen from behind with its paired foramina, where the sacral spinal nerves exit. It forms from five sacral vertebrae, a fusion that doesn't begin until after age 20.

title: Guess the body part
question: What are you looking at?
lines: Comment the second you know what this is.
This close up, it looks like a mountain range.
What are you looking at?
It's a big back tooth in the lower jaw, with several cusps.
Premolars sit in front of it, with just two rounded cusps.
It's D. A molar, the lower first molar.
Fun fact: adults have 12 molars, and four of them are wisdom teeth.
why: D) A molar (the lower first molar). Molars are the largest, most posterior teeth, with several cusps; premolars in front have two rounded cusps. Adults have 12 molars, including the 4 wisdom teeth.

title: Guess the body part
question: What are you looking at?
lines: Comment the second you know what this is.
A smooth ball of bone. Watch what it's attached to.
What are you looking at?
That ball fits into a socket in the hip.
The humerus has a ball too, but it's in the arm.
It's A. The femur, your thigh bone.
Fun fact: it's the longest and strongest bone in your body.
why: A) The femur. Its rounded head fits the hip bone's socket (the acetabulum) to form the hip joint. It's the longest and strongest bone of the body.

title: Guess the body part
question: Which part of the heart is this?
lines: Comment the second you know what this is.
We start on one smooth, curved wall of muscle.
Which part of the heart is this?
It's a big lower chamber, on the heart's left side.
The right ventricle is the lower chamber on the other side.
It's C. The left ventricle.
Fun fact: its wall is the thickest, to push blood around the whole body.
why: C) The left ventricle, the lower chamber on the heart's left side. Its muscle is much thicker than the right ventricle's because it pumps blood into the long systemic circuit.

title: Guess the body part
question: What are you looking at?
lines: Comment the second you know what this is.
A curved ridge of bone, up close. Keep watching.
What are you looking at?
That row of teeth sits in the lower jaw.
The maxilla holds the upper teeth. This bone is below it.
It's A. The mandible, your lower jaw.
Fun fact: it's the only bone in the skull that moves.
why: A) The mandible, the lower jaw, which anchors the lower teeth (the maxilla holds the upper ones). It is the only moveable bone of the skull.

title: Guess the body part
question: What are you looking at?
lines: Comment the second you know what this is.
Thick blocks of bone, stacked up. Watch it pull back.
What are you looking at?
These five sit just above the sacrum, in the lower back.
Thoracic vertebrae are higher up, where the ribs attach.
It's D. The lumbar vertebrae.
Fun fact: they carry the most weight, so they have the biggest bodies.
why: D) The lumbar vertebrae, L1 to L5, just above the sacrum. They carry the most body weight, so their vertebral bodies are the largest and thickest; thoracic vertebrae above them have sites for the ribs.

title: Guess the body part
question: What are you looking at?
lines: Comment the second you know what this is.
A long, smooth bone, up close. Watch it pull back.
What are you looking at?
Five long bones fan out from the wrist. This is the middle one.
Metatarsals look the same, but they're in the foot.
It's C. A metacarpal, the third one.
Fun fact: the far ends of your metacarpals are your knuckles.
why: C) A metacarpal (the third). The five metacarpals form the palm between the wrist bones and the fingers; metatarsals are the matching bones of the foot. Their distal ends form the knuckles.

title: Guess the body part
question: What are you looking at?
lines: Comment the second you know what this is.
A broad, flat sheet of bone. Watch it pull back.
What are you looking at?
It sits at the back of the shoulder, at the top of the arm.
The hip bone is broad and flat too, but it's in the pelvis.
It's B. The scapula, your shoulder blade.
Fun fact: it has no joint with your ribs. Muscles surround it instead.
why: B) The scapula (shoulder blade), at the back of the shoulder, meeting the humerus and the clavicle. It is surrounded by muscles and does not articulate with the ribs.
